Under-eye bags that are present regardless of sleep, salt or time of day generally relate to fat pad and tissue changes with age, and no cream addresses that — the honest options there are medical, and belong with a clinician.

sections.h: When puffiness is a medical matter
sections.body: Get urgent medical attention for sudden swelling of one eye, swelling with pain, redness, fever or any change in vision, or swelling that accompanies swelling of the lips or tongue or difficulty breathing. See a doctor for persistent puffiness that does not settle through the day, swelling that appeared with a new medication, or puffiness alongside changes in weight, urination or fatigue. Periorbital swelling occasionally reflects thyroid, kidney, cardiac or allergic conditions, and none of that is a skincare question.

fix.title: When a Retinoid Is Too Much for Your Skin
fix.h1: Your retinoid is too much: how to back off without abandoning it
fix.qa: Redness, flaking, stinging and tightness in the first weeks of a retinoid are common and usually a frequency problem rather than a reason to stop entirely. Reduce to twice a week, apply a moisturiser before and after, use a pea-sized amount on a dry face, and build back slowly over months. Persistent severe irritation, or anything with a prescription retinoid, is a conversation for the prescribing doctor.

sections.h: What is happening, and what 'retinisation' is worth
sections.body: Retinoids accelerate skin cell turnover, and the early weeks often bring dryness, flaking, redness and sensitivity while the surface adjusts. The industry calls this retinisation and treats it as a rite of passage. That framing is useful up to a point and abused past it — it has persuaded a great many people to push through reactions that were simply too much product too often. Discomfort is not evidence that it is working, and there is no prize for enduring it. Efficacy comes from consistent use over months, not from intensity.

sections.h: The adjustments that usually rescue it
sections.body: Drop to twice a week and hold there for a month before increasing. Use a genuinely pea-sized amount for the whole face. Apply to completely dry skin, since damp skin increases penetration and irritation. Sandwich it: moisturiser, retinoid, moisturiser. Keep it off the eyelids, the corners of the nose and the lip edges, which react first. Stop all acids and vitamin C while you settle, use them on alternate nights afterwards, and wear sunscreen every morning without exception, which matters more on a retinoid than off one.

sections.h: Strength, form and what Korean shelves offer
sections.body: Retinol, retinal and retinyl esters differ in how directly they act, with retinal generally regarded as more potent than retinol at comparable percentages, and esters as gentler and correspondingly less effective. Encapsulated forms are marketed as gentler and there is reasonable rationale for that, though the difference is easy to overstate. Korean formulations often pair a lower-strength retinoid with hydrating and calming ingredients, which suits people who found a Western high-percentage serum unmanageable. Bakuchiol is frequently offered as an alternative; the evidence base for it is much smaller and it is not a like-for-like substitute.

sections.h: When to stop and ask someone
sections.body: Stop and see a doctor if you develop persistent swelling, blistering, weeping, severe pain, or irritation that does not settle within a few days of stopping. If you are using a prescription retinoid such as tretinoin, any adjustment belongs with the doctor who prescribed it rather than with an article. Anyone pregnant, trying to conceive or breastfeeding should discuss retinoid use with a clinician before continuing — this is a well-established area of medical caution and not one to resolve by reading forums.

fix.title: When to Stop DIY and See a Professional
fix.h1: When to stop troubleshooting your routine and see a doctor
fix.qa: Stop experimenting and book an appointment if something is painful, spreading, blistering, weeping or swelling; if acne is cystic or leaving marks; if a rash keeps returning across unrelated products; if a patch has persisted for weeks despite a bland routine; or if a mole has changed. Skincare troubleshooting is for cosmetic concerns. A great many things that look cosmetic are diagnoses with treatments that no routine substitutes for.

sections.h: The urgent list
sections.body: Swelling of the lips, tongue or eyelids, difficulty breathing, or a rash spreading over the body needs emergency care, not a forum. So does sudden one-sided facial swelling with pain, any rapid change in vision, or signs of infection — spreading heat, yellow crusting, fever. Blistering, weeping or severe pain after a peel or a strong active also warrants same-day attention. None of these are situations where waiting to see whether a barrier cream helps is a reasonable plan, and the cost of being cautious here is very low.

sections.h: Things that are diagnoses, not skin types
sections.body: Rosacea, eczema, seborrhoeic dermatitis, perioral dermatitis, psoriasis, melasma, fungal folliculitis and contact allergy are all commonly self-labelled as sensitive skin, dryness, congestion or stubborn pigmentation. Several of them are made worse by exactly the products people reach for. Perioral dermatitis in particular is often aggravated by heavy creams and by steroid creams borrowed from a drawer. If your skin problem has a shape, a location and a persistence to it, the useful question is what it is, and that requires someone who can examine you.

sections.h: The slower signals people ignore
sections.body: Acne that is cystic, painful or leaving marks and scars deserves medical treatment now rather than after another six months of trials, because the marks are the part that is hard to undo. A patch that has not shifted in six weeks on a genuinely bland routine is not a routine problem. Reactions to multiple unrelated products point to a shared allergen and need proper patch testing. Hair loss, persistent itching, and any new, changing, bleeding or irregular mole all belong with a doctor promptly.

sections.h: Going in prepared
sections.body: Bring photographs of the problem at its worst, since skin has a habit of behaving in waiting rooms. Bring a list of every product you use, including hair products, and the packaging of anything you suspect — ingredient lists are genuinely useful to a dermatologist. Note when it started, what makes it better or worse, and what you have already tried and for how long. In Korea, dermatology clinics — 피부과 (pibugwa) — are widely accessible, but wherever you are, going earlier costs less than going later.
